lines.li: [them] I was one of the colony's own, back when {TOWN} was {OLDCOLONY}.
[us] What was it like?
[them,town:struggling|town:poor] Better fed than we are now, and loud at supper.
[them] Busy, and loud at supper, and I would not trade a day of it.
[us] How long is it now since the hand-over?
[them] {YEARSSINCE}, and the place still feels like {OLDCOLONY} to me.
[us] Do they still call it that?
[them,their:lowtech] The old ones do, by the fire, when the young ones are asleep.
[them] Only the ones who were there, and we are fewer every year.
[them] I think about you every day out at {TOWN}, you know.
[us] I think about you too.
[them] Living in two places is hard, however right it was for the town.
[us] Do you still do things the way the colony did?
[them,their:tribal] We keep the old fire as it was kept, and we still sit the same way around it.
[them,their:medieval] Aye, the meeting in the hall in the evening, and the charter read on its day.
[them,their:spacer] Mostly, though the administration has added a few procedures of its own.
[them] Mostly, though we have picked up a few habits of our own since.
[us] You're from {TOWN}?
[them,their:medieval] Aye, and it was {OLDCOLONY} once, your colony's, before it was ours.
[them] That's right, the town that used to be {OLDCOLONY}.
[us] How do they remember us there?
[them,tone:warm|tone:good] Kindly, the old ones speak of your people as old friends.
[them] As the ones who built the place, mostly.
[them] It has been hard at {TOWN} lately.
[us] If the colony can help, write to us.
[them] We might, and it is good to know the door is open.
[them] {TOWN} is doing well, you would hardly know it for {OLDCOLONY}.
[us] Good, it deserves to.
[them,them:former] It does, and you lot gave it a good start.
[them] Your people gave it a good start, so the old ones say.
